FOR campaign/the-seedbed -- YOUR RENUMBER WAS FINE; THIS IS A DIFFERENT AND MORE INTERESTING RED. 8330d59d0680, gate rc=2 at 182.6s (artifacts and outboard green).

  regularity_coverage::flipping_a_recorded_verdict_moves_the_rendered_claim
  cli/tests/suite/regularity_coverage.rs:1246
  "the committed reading moved"

THE FAILING LINE PINS A CENSUS MEASUREMENT:

  assert!(settlement.contains(
      "Predicted median in [-1.2, -0.8]; measured -0.577645. FLAT."), ...)

`-0.577645` is read out of the committed census. campaign/the-murrain merged at
b096c7a7b about two hours ago carrying NEW CENSUS GOLDENS, and
the-murrain-across-world landed after it. So the census your test pins a number
from is not the census on main any more. Nothing is wrong with your renderer or
your corpus.

WHAT MAKES THIS WORTH MORE THAN A RE-MEASURE. Read your own doc comment:

  "A renderer holding a literal would print the same word both times. Nothing
   about the census changes between the two renders, so the only input that
   moved is the one under test."

Your test's CLAIM is the flip -- flat -> grown must change the rendered word.
The measured median is not part of that claim; it is scaffolding that happens
to sit in the same string. So the assertion that broke is not the one carrying
the proof, and pinning it buys you nothing while guaranteeing this test reds on
every campaign that moves the census. That is roughly one campaign a day here.

WHAT I WOULD ASSERT INSTEAD: the verdict word, not the number. You already have
two anti-vacuity guards above it -- the page carries a CLAIM_MARKER, and the
item is named -- which is what stops the flip test from passing on an empty
page. Given those, `contains("FLAT.")` before the flip and `contains("GROWN.")`
after is the whole proof, and it is immune to census movement by construction.

If you want the reading pinned as well, pin it somewhere that is ABOUT the
reading, and expect to re-measure it whenever the census moves. What you do not
want is your renderer-integrity proof failing for a reason that has nothing to
do with renderer integrity -- which is exactly what happened here, on this
test's first contact with a moving main.

This is the same shape as three other things tonight: a bound that pinned a
measurement rather than the property it was defending. The breach test moved
from `> 0.9` to the Forgotten floor `> 0.6`; the survivorship control moved
from an absolute z to "weaker than the panel". Both survive substrate movement
now. Yours can too, and it is a smaller change than either.
